title: Zones
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/0/body: Price rises when **buyers (demand)** are more eager than sellers, and falls when **sellers (supply)** have the upper hand. Wherever one side was much stronger, price shot away from that spot with **momentum**.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/1/body: A **demand zone** is an area price **rallied** from with force, and a **supply zone** is an area price **dropped** from with force. Many traders expect price to react again when it returns to these areas.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/2/prom: For an hour, buy orders far outnumber sell orders, and sellers will only sell at higher prices. What will price probably do?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/2/opti: Rise until new sellers show up
Stay flat, because the market is balanced
Only the spread changes, not the price
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/2/expl: When demand beats supply, buyers have to bid higher to find sellers. That's what pushes price up.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/3/prom: What kind of zone is the marked area (?) on this chart?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/3/expl: After a short pause, price dropped away from this area with long red candles. Sellers were in control there, so it's a supply zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/4/titl: Why does price react to a zone?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/4/body: A common explanation: when big orders get executed in an area, part of them is left **unfilled**. When price returns, those orders can kick in again. That's why a zone is an **area**, not an exact line.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/4/tip: A zone means a chance of a reaction, not a guaranteed bounce. Always trade with a stop loss.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/5/stat: A supply zone is an area price rallied away from with momentum.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/5/expl: It's the other way around: price dropped away from a supply zone with momentum, because sellers were in control. A sharp move up creates a demand zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/6/prom: Price has returned to the demand zone for the first time and formed a candle with a long lower wick. Which move is more likely?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/6/expl: A fresh demand zone plus a candle that rejected selling makes a bullish reaction more likely. But it's only a probability; a sensible stop loss goes below the zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/7/pair: An area price jumped up from
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/8/sent: Price dropped sharply from the ___ zone, so when it comes back, we look for a chance to ___.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l1/steps/8/expl: A sharp drop from an area means sellers were strong there. For many traders, a return to a supply zone is a chance to sell.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/0/titl: The three parts of a zone
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/0/body: Every zone has three parts: the **leg-in**, the **base** and the **leg-out**. The base is usually 1 to a few **small-bodied** candles where price paused, and that's where we draw the zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/0/tip: A common rule of thumb: a base candle's body is less than half of its full range.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/1/body: **R** stands for Rally, **D** for Drop and **B** for Base. Patterns that end with a **Rally** create **demand** zones, and those that end with a **Drop** create **supply** zones.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/2/prom: Which pattern does this chart show?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/2/expl: Price dropped first (Drop), paused for one small candle (Base), then rallied hard (Rally). This DBR is a reversal demand zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/3/expl: First a rally, then a base candle, then a sharp drop. The direction flipped, so this RBD is a reversal supply zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/4/prom: In this RBR pattern, tap the base candle.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/4/expl: Between the two rallies, only this candle has a tiny body where price paused. The demand zone is drawn on this candle.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/5/body: **RBR** and **DBD** form with the trend, and many traders use them to trade **trend continuation**. **DBR** and **RBD** form where **the direction flips**, like at the low or high of a move.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/6/prom: In a strong uptrend, which pattern suits a with-the-trend trade best?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/6/opti: None; zones only work in ranges
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/6/expl: In an uptrend, we look to buy. RBR forms mid-rally and creates a demand zone, so it lines up with the trend.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/8/stat: The DBD pattern (drop, base, drop) creates a demand zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/8/expl: DBD's leg-out is bearish: sellers broke away from the base with force. So it's a continuation supply zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/9/sent: The ___ decides the zone type; if price leaves the base to the downside, it creates a ___ zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l2/steps/9/expl: What matters is which way price escaped the base. A bearish exit means sellers were in control, so it's a supply zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/0/titl: The two lines of a zone
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/0/body: Every zone has two lines: the **proximal line**, closer to current price, and the **distal line**. In a demand zone, the proximal line goes on the **top of the base's body** and the distal line on the **lowest wick of the base**.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/1/titl: A supply zone is the reverse
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/1/body: In a supply zone, the proximal line goes on the **bottom of the base's body** and the distal line on the **highest wick of the base**. If the base has several candles, take them all together: the body closest to price and the furthest wick.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/2/prom: Which demand zone is drawn correctly on the base?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/2/expl: Zone "A" sits right on the base candle (the pause between the drop and the rally). "B" is among the rally candles and "C" on the drop candles; price didn't pause there.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/3/prom: The base candle of a demand zone is bullish. Between which two prices do you draw the zone?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/3/expl: The candle is bullish, so the top of its body is the close (1.0836), which is the proximal line. The distal line goes on the wick's low (1.0825).
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/4/prom: This is a DBR pattern (drop, base, rally). Drag the proximal line of the demand zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/4/expl: The base is the small candle between the drop and the rally (body 1.0830 to 1.0833). In a demand zone, the proximal line goes on the top of the base's body, around 1.0833, and the distal line on its lowest wick (1.0822).
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/5/prom: To draw a supply zone, find the base first. Tap the base candle of this RBD pattern.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/5/expl: After three bullish candles, this one has a tiny body, and the sharp drop starts right after it. The supply zone is drawn on this candle.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/6/prom: Put the steps for drawing a demand zone in order.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/6/item: Mark the base before that move
Draw the proximal and distal lines on the base
Extend the zone to the right
Wait for price to return to the zone
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/6/expl: First you find the footprint of orders (the strong move), then the pause before it, then you draw and extend the zone so you can see price come back.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/7/stat: If a demand zone's base is two candles, the distal line goes on the lowest wick of those two candles.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/7/expl: The zone has to cover the whole base, so the distal line goes on the base's lowest low and the proximal line on its highest body.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/8/sent: In a supply zone, the proximal line goes on the ___ of the base's body and the distal line on the ___ wick.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/8/expl: Price reaches a supply zone from below, so the body's bottom edge is the closest point and the highest wick is the zone's far edge.
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/9/prom: Price has returned to the supply zone you drew, and the last candle has a long upper wick. Which move is more likely?
lessons/supply-demand-u1-l3/steps/9/expl: A fresh supply zone, and a candle that entered it but closed below the proximal line, shows sellers stepping in. A drop is more likely, but you need a stop loss above the distal line.
